For here, just as in many other places, whatever profit is collected returns entirely to the King. Adjacent to this place are the workshops of the goldsmiths, whose consul keeps the seal and the dies of the currency. In Fez, neither a ring nor any other object can be manufactured from gold or silver unless the metal has first been sealed: for they punish those who transgress this law most severely. Once the metal is sealed, whatever is made from it is spent as if it were currency. However, the greater part of the goldsmiths who inhabit New Fez consists of Jews, and they carry their golden and silver vessels to a certain place in Old Fez, situated not far from the spice merchants, to sell them. For in Old Fez, neither gold nor silver is minted, nor is it permitted for Muhammadans <note>original: "Mahumetanis"</note> to practice this craft, because they have usurers who resell any silver or gold work for more than the value of its weight, although this is permitted to the Jews by the rulers of the city.
